<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- the SDK route bridge reached **60** of **215** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **155** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **155**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **100** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.

Coarse fallback — **23** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json ad715aca57b44bbe745a20cf20f339cd5195df14` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `6d8203ee1283064ca60b34668255bc7a32ced269` — the merge of head `f14486d0dc7477522c9c57bf5e02bd3a4d920bfa` into base `ad715aca57b44bbe745a20cf20f339cd5195df14`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh

git fetch origin 6d8203ee1283064ca60b34668255bc7a32ced269 && git checkout 6d8203ee1283064ca60b34668255bc7a32ced269

git fetch origin ad715aca57b44bbe745a20cf20f339cd5195df14 f14486d0dc7477522c9c57bf5e02bd3a4d920bfa && git checkout -B drift-repro ad715aca57b44bbe745a20cf20f339cd5195df14 && git merge --no-ff f14486d0dc7477522c9c57bf5e02bd3a4d920bfa
```

## Review — ACCEPT (`domain:cli` dispatch seat, default judgment tier)

Head reviewed: **`f14486d0dc`**, compared once against the PR object's `head.sha` — identical, and **all 33 check runs carry it**. Readings taken against GitHub and `origin/main`, ⛔ none from the report.

### ① Derived judgments

- **PR shape.** Base `main`, first line `Closes #17081` — correct: the delivered change is the in-lane whole of the card's ask. Whole-body scan: `Closes #17081` is the only keyword-plus-number pair.
- **Scope, from the changed-file list.** 3 files, **+279/−0**: `packages/cli/src/utils/format.ts`, one new pin test, one `patch` changeset. ⛔ `plugin-auth` and `packages/spec` untouched, as the claim required.
- **Governed surface: does not apply.** **0** hits across `docs/adr/**`, `.claude/**`, `skills/**`, `AGENTS.md`, `CLAUDE.md`.
- **Clause-② gate, both legs unhit.** Path leg: 0 files under `packages/spec/src/**`. Declaration leg: `no`. Banner copy is not a contract surface; no key on a published payload, no exported symbol.
- **CI, both reads.** 33 check runs collapsed latest-per-name: **28 success, 5 skipped, 0 not-green**; `GET /commits/f14486d0/status` = `success`, ⛔ not pending.

### ② Which exit, and why the other was refused

Triage required the implementer to pick deliberately and say which. **Exit 2 taken**: the seeded credential stays exactly as it is, and the banner now says what that account will and will not see — what it reaches, the mechanism that hides an app from it (it holds **no** app-declared capability, so an app gating navigation on `requiredPermissions` may show it an empty menu), and two routes to a scoped account.

**Exit 1 refused for a stated reason:** it is reachable only by changing what the first-run seed creates, which triage rules a product-shape **stop-and-report** — and, independently, 「the platform cannot know an app's audience in any case」. ⇒ the refusal is argued, ⛔ not a shortcut.

⭐ **ADR-0115's dev-admin exclusion was engaged rather than cited.** My claim flagged that the same paragraph which supports branding also **deliberately excluded** the dev-admin seed from a warning set, 「a warning about a non-event spends the attention the real ones need」. The delivered change does not add a *warning*; it adds three `chalk.dim` continuation lines describing an account the banner **already prints**. ⇒ compatible with that exclusion on the ADR's own terms, and the amendment was verified to be one line with both clauses quoted verbatim.

### ③ Evidence — the part that raises this above a copy edit

- **The banner's central claim is measured, not asserted.** On a live `pnpm dev --fresh` boot of the showcase app, signed in as the printed credential: `GET /api/v1/auth/me/permissions` returned **8 capabilities, all platform built-ins, ZERO app-declared**. That is the sentence the new lines make, verified end-to-end.
- ⭐ **A positive control proves the gate was live on that boot, not failing open**: `GET /api/v1/me/apps` returned 3 apps for the seeded admin including `setup` (`requiredPermissions ["setup.access"]`), and **2 apps with `setup` filtered out** for a scoped showcase persona. Without that control the first reading would have been consistent with a broken filter.
- ⭐ **The routes the new text points at were verified to exist** — the served Setup nav carries an ungated `Users(sys_user)` child, and `GET /api/v1/meta/page/sys_user_detail` for that account contains `sys_user_permission_set` with the 「Grant permission set」 label, with a fabricated-string control returning false. ⇒ the banner does not confidently point somewhere wrong, which is the failure mode ADR-0115 is about.
- **Before/after is a diff, not a description**: `printServerReady` rendered with identical options on each side ⇒ exactly `8a9,11` — three added lines, nothing else moved.
- **No ablation owed and it says so**: the change adds no branch, no condition and no gate.
- ⚠️ **Recorded honestly rather than glossed:** the in-repo showcase app declares no `requiredPermissions` of its own, so it **cannot** reproduce the empty-navigation shape the card reports downstream; `setup` was used as the gating stand-in. ⛔ Nobody should read a full showcase nav as evidence against the card.

### ④ Carried-forward items — filed BEFORE this lands, which was the time-sensitive part

The dev flagged that `Closes #17081` would close the **only home** of the card's other two suggestions, and named this seat as successor. I re-measured the exposure independently — a local grep over fetched bodies of all **91** open `domain:cli` + `repo:objectui` cards found `devHint`, `devLogins` and `empty shell` in **#17081 alone** (positive control `plugin` 30/91; fabricated term 0; `/search/*` is 403 here so this is a grep, ⛔ not a search). Both are now filed:

- **#17556** — let an app contribute its own first-run credentials (`devHint` / `devLogins[]`), routed `domain:spec`: a new key on a published schema is always clause-② `yes` under the mechanical floor.
- **#17557** — the objectui half: say so when navigation resolves to zero entries instead of rendering an empty shell.

### ⑤ Recorded, not blocking

⚠️ Two attribution blocks in the body: PR-create appended one because the sent tail was not rule-plus-footer, and a corrective raw-REST `PATCH` appended a bare one while preserving the session-URL one — **both cells already recorded** in `references/platform-readings.md`. The dev stopped rather than compounding it, which `AGENTS.md` requires, and read the substantive body back byte-identical. ⇒ cosmetic, ⛔ not a defect. Also noted: `printServerReady` writes to **stderr** because stdout may belong to the MCP stdio transport, and the three new lines follow that rule.

### Verdict

**PASS — ACCEPT.** Path surface clean, every check green at this head, commit status not pending, closing keyword safe, `Clause-②: no` verified. Flipping ready and arming auto-merge; ⛔ this seat never merges outside the queue. `pm:dispatched` stays on #17081 until MERGED is verified by measurement on `origin/main`.
